title: Summer squash, yellow or green, fresh, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (Cucurbita pepo) is the immature fruit of the squash plant, usually yellow or green. Fresh fruits are tender, juicy, and have a mild flavor. Cooking them in butter or margarine preserves their natural sweetness and gives a silky texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the cucurbit family, close to zucchini, pumpkins, and cucumbers.
Unlike many vegetables, both the flesh and the skin of summer squash are edible.
Yellow varieties arise from natural genetic variation, not from added colorants.
They are used worldwide: in Italy for ratatouille, in Japan for tempura, and in the US for fried sticks.
Fresh summer squash is about 95 % water, so it loses moisture quickly if stored too long.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: With only about 17 kcal per 100 g, summer squash is an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and enhances iron absorption.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related degeneration.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, wash thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

items.title: Nutrient loss with over‑cooking
items.content: Excessive high‑heat cooking can degrade heat‑sensitive vitamins, especially vitamin C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Summer squash can be sautéed, stewed, roasted, or steamed. Cooking it in butter or margarine adds a rich flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins. Slice into cubes or rounds, add to stews, omelets, pasta dishes, or serve as a simple side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store summer squash in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or container, where it stays fresh for up to 5 days. Keep it away from ethylene‑producing fruits, which accelerate ripening. Rinse under running water before cooking.
